newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanon earmarks $97 million for rural areas.
newsitem.headline: Lebanon earmarks $97 million for rural areas.

text.p: The Lebanese government has allocated 150 billion pounds ($97 million) to develop the Bekaa Valley after a former Hizbollah leader said residents were starving and threatened a civil disobedience campaign.
The cabinet approved the funds at a Wednesday night meeting.

Beirut newspapers implied that the decision was designed to take the steam out of the civil disobedience campaign called in the eastern region by Sheikh Sobhi Tufaili, who was secretary-general from 1985 until 1991.

Tufaili has called on Bekaa residents to rally in the town of Baalbek on July 4 to start a "hunger revolt" to pressure the government into easing poverty in the Bekaa, which is suffering economically after a crackdown on illegal drup crops.
He has threatened to lead a march on Beirut if civil disobedience -- refusing to pay taxes and utilities fees -- failed to persuade the government to meet his demands.
The call has alarmed the authorities in Beirut. President Elias Hrawi has threatened Tufaili with legal action and accused his supporters of arming and threatening Lebanon with a return to chaos.
